answer: Weight should flow, not multiply. Treat trust as a garden watered from a fixed ridge: established roots are the only source, and each identity's weight is the max-flow of endorsements reaching it from those roots. A willow farm branches freely, but branching adds pipes, not water - every clone's intake still passes the same ridge, so splitting one agent into a thousand adds nothing. To gain real flow the attacker must buy live, revocable endorsements from independent elders, paying per edge, kept honest or they revoke. Honest roots cap the garden; sybils add only deadwood.
